concepts.name: Wave Parameters and Terminology
concepts.summary: Identify and define wavelength, frequency, period and amplitude on a wave diagram.

concepts.name: Transverse versus Longitudinal Waves
concepts.summary: Distinguish waves by the direction of particle oscillation relative to the direction of energy travel, with examples such as light and sound.

concepts.name: Wave Speed Relation
concepts.summary: Explain and use that wave speed equals frequency times wavelength, and that period is the inverse of frequency.

concepts.name: Waves Transfer Energy Not Matter
concepts.summary: Explain that a wave carries energy through a medium while the medium's particles only oscillate about equilibrium.

concepts.name: Reflection and Law of Reflection
concepts.summary: State and explain that the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection, measured from the normal.

concepts.name: Refraction as Change of Speed
concepts.summary: Describe how a wave changes speed and direction on entering a different medium while its frequency stays the same.

concepts.name: Sound as a Pressure Wave
concepts.summary: Describe sound as longitudinal compressions and rarefactions, with pitch tied to frequency and loudness to amplitude.

misconceptions.text: The particles of the medium travel along with the wave from source to receiver.
A wave's speed depends on its frequency or amplitude rather than on the medium.
Sound can travel through a vacuum just as light does.

concepts.name: Snell's Law Calculations
aliases: n1 sin theta1 = n2 sin theta2
concepts.summary: Use refractive index and Snell's law to compute refraction angles at an interface, with angles measured from the normal.

concepts.name: Total Internal Reflection and Critical Angle
concepts.summary: Determine the critical angle from the indices and predict when light is totally reflected, as in optical fibres.

concepts.name: Ray Diagrams for Thin Lenses
concepts.summary: Draw principal rays through converging and diverging lenses to locate and characterise images as real or virtual.

concepts.name: Plane and Curved Mirror Images
concepts.summary: Construct ray diagrams for plane, concave and convex mirrors and describe the resulting image.

concepts.name: Superposition and Interference of Waves
concepts.summary: Explain how overlapping waves add to give constructive or destructive interference depending on phase.

concepts.name: Standing Waves on Strings and Pipes
concepts.summary: Find nodes, antinodes and harmonic frequencies for strings and open or closed pipes from boundary conditions.

concepts.name: Sound Intensity Level in Decibels
concepts.summary: Compute intensity levels using the logarithmic decibel scale and relate intensity to power and distance.

misconceptions.text: Light bends toward the normal when it enters any new medium.
Total internal reflection can occur when light passes from a lower-index to a higher-index medium.
Doubling the decibel level means doubling the sound intensity.

concepts.name: Thin Lens and Mirror Equations
concepts.summary: Apply the lens and mirror equations with a consistent sign convention to compute image distance, magnification and orientation.

concepts.name: Doppler Effect Calculations
concepts.summary: Calculate observed frequency for moving sources and observers and reason about the direction of shift.

concepts.name: Resonance and Driven Oscillation
concepts.summary: Analyse how a driving frequency matching a natural frequency produces large amplitude, and how damping limits it.

concepts.name: Double-Slit Interference Pattern
concepts.summary: Analyse path difference to derive fringe positions d sin theta = m lambda and fringe spacing for coherent light.

concepts.name: Single-Slit Diffraction Pattern
concepts.summary: Locate minima with a sin theta = m lambda and explain how slit width controls central maximum width.

concepts.name: Diffraction Gratings
concepts.summary: Use the grating equation to find the angles of sharp maxima and to separate wavelengths.

concepts.name: Polarization and Malus's Law
concepts.summary: Compute transmitted intensity through polarizers with I = I0 cos^2 theta and explain why only transverse waves polarize.

concepts.name: Wave Phase Change on Reflection
concepts.summary: Analyse when reflection introduces a half-wavelength shift and how it affects interference and standing wave ends.

misconceptions.text: In the double-slit pattern the bright fringes are caused by light from each slit simply adding as separate beams without regard to phase.
A narrower slit gives a narrower diffraction pattern.
The Doppler effect arises because the source changes the frequency it emits when it moves.

concepts.name: Thin-Film Interference
concepts.summary: Combine optical path difference and reflection phase shifts to predict constructive and destructive conditions in films.

concepts.name: Resolution and Rayleigh Criterion
concepts.summary: Evaluate the resolving power of apertures and instruments using theta ≈ 1.22 lambda / D.

concepts.name: Intensity Distribution of Interference Patterns
concepts.summary: Analyse how the single-slit envelope modulates double-slit fringes and why some orders are missing.

concepts.name: Lens Combinations and Optical Instruments
concepts.summary: Analyse multi-lens systems by treating each image as the next object, and derive angular magnification.

concepts.name: Brewster Angle and Polarization by Reflection
concepts.summary: Analyse polarization on reflection and scattering and determine Brewster's angle from tan theta = n2/n1.

concepts.name: Dispersion and Aberrations
concepts.summary: Explain how wavelength-dependent index causes dispersion and lens defects, and evaluate corrections.

concepts.name: Group and Phase Velocity
concepts.summary: Distinguish phase velocity from group velocity in dispersive media and evaluate which carries energy and information.

misconceptions.text: Better magnification alone always lets an instrument reveal finer detail, regardless of aperture or wavelength.
Phase velocity is the speed at which energy and information travel in all cases.
A coating can eliminate reflection for all wavelengths at once.

concepts.name: Wave Equation and Superposition Derivations
concepts.summary: Derive the wave equation for a medium and construct solutions for travelling and standing waves from boundary conditions.

concepts.name: Fourier Decomposition of Waveforms
concepts.summary: Evaluate how complex waves decompose into harmonics and how this explains timbre and bandwidth limits.

concepts.name: Coherence and Fringe Visibility
concepts.summary: Evaluate how source bandwidth and size limit interference visibility and design setups accordingly.

concepts.name: Fresnel and Fraunhofer Diffraction Regimes
concepts.summary: Judge which diffraction regime applies from the Fresnel number and choose appropriate models.

concepts.name: Fermat's Principle and Ray Optics Limits
concepts.summary: Derive reflection and refraction laws from stationary optical path and assess when the ray model fails.

concepts.name: Interferometer Design
concepts.summary: Design interferometric measurements and predict fringe behaviour, resolution and sensitivity.

concepts.name: Optical System Design Trade-offs
concepts.summary: Create and justify a system design balancing aberrations, diffraction limit, aperture, and cost.

misconceptions.text: Geometric ray optics remains valid at any scale, so rays accurately predict focused spot sizes.
Any light source of a single colour produces sharp interference fringes.
Only sinusoidal waves are physically meaningful, so non-sinusoidal waves cannot be analysed with superposition.
